en.title: Maximum Matching Positions After Transferring Non-negative Inventory
en.description:
You are given two arrays inv1 and inv2 of equal length. Any number of times, you may choose distinct i and j and, only when inv1[j]>0, take 1 from j and add 1 to i. Inventory may become 0 after the operations but never negative; inv2 does not change. The similarity is the number of indices whose values are equal in both arrays. Find the maximum similarity.

The standard I/O, examples and editorial were written independently by this site; ranges explicitly marked as this site's are not the source's original constraints.
en.input: The first line contains n, the second line contains inv1, and the third line contains inv2. 1≤n≤100000; every value in both initial arrays is in 1..10000.
en.output: Output a single integer, the answer.
en.explanation: The answers are 0, 2 and 2 respectively. You cannot keep taking from a position whose inventory is 0, so in the first example the budget is not enough to match any 4; in the third example the extra total of 9 must go to at least one unmatched position.
hints: The total inventory S never changes. If it equals the target sum, every position can be matched; otherwise, go through target values from smallest to largest and use the budget S to match as many positions as possible, but at most n−1. Implement it with counting buckets over the value range 10000.
